question: Do our own margin projections beat predicting nothing, out of sample?
status: Answered — yes for three rules, but not decisively
known_facts_verified: Eight competing rules were evaluated on 96 unseen games. Three (S5, S6, S7) beat the zero baseline with a 95% interval entirely above zero; the strongest of those is S6 at 7.1% error reduction, interval [0.4%, 13.8%], winner accuracy 67.0%, Brier 0.2284 against a 0.25 coin-flip baseline. The highest raw score, S4 at 7.7%, has an interval crossing zero.
missing_information: More weeks, and a pre-registered rule set so new rules are not chosen after seeing scores. No rule currently survives the multiple-comparison adjustment.
how_to_discover_official_first: Re-run scripts/model.py as official weeks are added.

question: Does simply backing the home team every week work?

missing_information: Nothing further; the answer is stable enough to act on for this sample.
how_to_discover_official_first: Re-test each season; home advantage has changed over time.

missing_information: A larger sample and better features (pace, weather, venue, officiating tendencies) would be needed before trusting a total.
how_to_discover_official_first: Re-run scripts/model.py as official weeks are added.

question: How often must the line book be captured so a closing number exists for every originated market?

missing_information: Nobody has decided when a capture happens. The store can record an interim or closing snapshot, but nothing runs it, so every closing number will be missing at kickoff unless a cadence is agreed.
how_to_discover_official_first: Set the cadence in the project itself (for example: capture at line publication, at T-24h, and at T-2h before each kickoff), then the store's own contract check reports any market that reached kickoff uncaptured.

question: What payout assumption may the staking ledger publish, given there is no market price?
status: Open - current answer is a declared flat assumption
known_facts_verified: data/staking_book.csv computes units at 1 unit won / 1 unit lost against the project reference line; M1 36-14 and M2 41-17 reproduce the published hit rates exactly, and the best run in the family (+24 units) is reached by chance in 0.4% of no-skill simulations across 6-7 strategies.
missing_information: Any number that looks like a return (ROI, 'profit', break-even percentage) invites a reader to compare it with a bookmaker's result. It cannot be compared: there is no price (F07), and in NL and Japan the presentation of return figures may itself matter (F09, F19).
how_to_discover_official_first: Owner decision, informed by the legal review already flagged; no new source is needed to answer it.

question: Which strategies will be gated on a rolling window, and over what window length?
status: Open - one window implemented, its behaviour measured
known_facts_verified: D1 as drafted (lower 95% bound of the recent-50 advantage above zero) fires for all four ridge variants today: measured advantages are +0.74 (M1), +0.59 (M2), +0.31 (M3) and +0.77 (M4) points with intervals that all include zero. Session 8a0bf37e's demotion_window_check.csv reaches the same conclusion independently.
missing_information: A gate that fires on almost every strategy at n=50 is either correctly strict or wrongly specified, and the difference has to be decided before it can demote anything: what window, what interval level, and whether a demotion needs both the rolling and the full-window test to fail.
how_to_discover_official_first: No external source needed - this is a threshold decision. The evidence for it is already in the repository (data/demotion_evaluation.csv, data/demotion_window_check.csv).

question: What is the minimum n at which this project will publish a correlation at all?
status: Open - floors are now published beside every value
known_facts_verified: The register prints, for each row, the smallest |r| the sample could have found at 80% power: 0.237 at n=137, 0.293 at n=89, 0.545 at n=24, 0.567 at n=22. Two rows are blank by rule because no settled sample exists yet (availability against outcomes, replacement depth against outcomes).
missing_information: Without a stated minimum, a reader can mistake 'no significant correlation at n=24' for 'independence', when the sample could only have found a very large association. CR06 is the live example: the sign is stable, the size swings from -0.299 to -0.365 on a definitional choice.
how_to_discover_official_first: No new source needed - the floors are computed from the samples already in the repository; the owner only has to set the cut-off.
